comments.author: kdamken
comments.why: Argues employers should pay a living wage instead of tips
comments.text: Tipping is the worst possible thing for everyone involved. Your employer should be paying you a living wage, not expecting the customers to do so with tips. I highly recommend you check out this video: [VIDEO] Tipping doesn't really say much about a person other than how easily they fall for societal pressure and guilt.

comments.author: FactolSarin
comments.story: What Minimum-Wage Foes Got Wrong About Seattle
comments.text: If the large chain won't adjust, that seems something that would give smaller businesses an advantage, and seems like a positive to my ears. As for tipping, people don't tend to tip based on quality of service (see Adam Ruins Everything) [ [VIDEO] ], and instead tends to be based more on attractiveness and ethnicity. A normal wage is fairer.

comments.author: pedalpete
comments.story: Why the Restaurant Industry Hates Postmates
comments.why: Tipping culture as root of the food-service wage problem
comments.text: Isn't this article really more about the problem with the food service industry relying on tips instead of paying their workers a proper wage. [VIDEO] Postmates isn't intentionally preying on the industry, the industry was set-up this way, with the expectation of tips being paid by customers, but the model is changing. If the restaurants charged the actual price they expect to get for their product, then the issue would become what the couriers get paid, which may be too low, but then the market would/should decide on what is fair.
